methodological_rigor.justification: In vitro functional assays (viability, colony formation, invasion, cell cycle, Western blotting) appropriate for mechanism elucidation. Clear FH535 dose-response evaluation and siRNA pathway validation. Lacks animal models, human tissue validation, or statistical power documentation. Limited experimental replication detail.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Basic science in vitro only. No animal models, xenografts, or patient samples. Immune implications speculative without functional immune cell studies. No translational pathway defined.

reporting_quality.justification: Limited methods detail. No data/reagent availability statement. Incomplete control descriptions and reproducibility information.

novelty_literature.justification: Wnt/β-catenin inhibition previously characterized. Chemokine modulation adds limited novelty. Incremental contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Readable but methods sparse. Discussion contextualizes findings. Immune claims speculative.

key_strengths: FH535-mediated Wnt inhibition demonstrated across multiple functional endpoints
Complementary pharmacological and genetic (siRNA) pathway validation
Systematic assessment of cell growth, migration, and invasion
key_concerns: No animal model or in vivo validation
Immune implications entirely speculative; no immune cell function studies
Limited mechanistic insight into MCP1/MCP2 modulation
Single cell line representation limits generalizability
chief_reviewer.rationale: Limited in vitro mechanistic study requiring animal validation for translational relevance. Appropriate for tier 4 pending in vivo studies.
